items.title: Prefix sum: range queries O(1) mein
items.one_idea: Build a running-total array once in O(n); then the sum of any range left..right is one subtraction, prefix[right+1] - prefix[left], so every query costs O(1) instead of a loop.

items.visual_idea: Six cells 3 1 4 1 5 9 with a second row below filling left to right with running totals 0 3 4 8 9 14 23; then a bracket over indices 2 to 4 lights the two prefix cells 14 and 4 and one subtraction 14 - 4 = 10 appears; last panel compares a loop re-adding the bracket every query with a single subtraction.

items.example: EXAMPLE array [3,1,4,1,5,9]; prefix [0,3,4,8,9,14,23]; sum of indices 2..4 = 4+1+5 = 10 = prefix[5] - prefix[2] = 14 - 4; whole array 23. For n = 100000 numbers and 100000 queries, worst-case brute force is 10,000,000,000 additions vs 100,000 for the build plus 100,000 subtractions. Real output of the planner's run.
items.pattern: precompute running totals, answer by subtraction
items.check_question: With prefix [0,3,4,8,9,14,23], what is the sum of indices 1..3? (6, since 9 - 3)
items.cover_headline: Prefix sum: range sums in O(1)
facts_to_verify: Prefix sum = running total, each output the sum of the inputs up to and including that index (Wikipedia Prefix sum, fetched)

Range sum = prefix[right+1] - prefix[left] with a leading 0; build O(n) time, query O(1), O(n) extra space (doocs 0303, fetched). The Wikipedia page does NOT state the range formula or the O(1) claim: cite doocs for it
Subtraction needs an operator with an inverse (works for sum, not for max): say so only if the script mentions other operators
Run the code and show its real output: prefix [0,3,4,8,9,14,23], sum 2..4 = 10 via 14 - 4, brute force equals prefix for every range (assert passed)
100000 x 100000 = 10,000,000,000 is arithmetic (worst case, every query spans the whole array); label it EXAMPLE
Paraphrase the problem; do not copy the doocs or LeetCode wording. The check question needs the answer 6 (prefix[4]-prefix[1] = 9-3)
